target_customer: Content creators and small online businesses
problem: Creators have one link in their social bio and no easy way to monetize or run a business from it. Beacons gives them a mobile site builder with store, email and media kit tools.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with paid premium plans (about $10 per month in 2021) and commerce fees
product_category: Creator economy, link-in-bio website and business platform

founders.name: David Zeng
education: PhD, Stanford (signal processing and machine learning for medical imaging)

founders.name: Greg Luppescu
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in a search summary of Beacons' seed announcement; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Linktree
competitors.what: Market-leading link-in-bio page aggregating a creator's social profiles
competitors.traction_then: Over 10 million users per a 2021 report

competitors.name: Linkin.bio, Lnk.bio, Shorby, Tap.bio and others
competitors.what: Smaller link-in-bio tools named by TechCrunch as rivals

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile-first block-based page builder with commerce integrations is standard web engineering for a technical team.

defensibility.rationale: Sacra notes the core link-in-bio product is commoditizing with 40+ competitors; differentiation came from block-based building and creator business tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Linktree and later Shopify Linkpop competed directly; Beacons still raised follow-on rounds but was not acquired.

market_need_then: Creators needed to monetize beyond a single bio link; Linktree had over 10 million users by 2021 and Beacons launched into a fast-growing creator economy.

branding.domain_note: Uses the .ai domain beacons.ai; BEACONS word mark filed July 2020 and registered February 2021

identity.voice_and_tone: Creator-friendly, positioning as an all-in-one business platform

branding.community_and_virality: Sacra and TechCrunch cover growth driven by creator word of mouth; The Chainsmokers invested as brand-adjacent creators.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong creator adoption and press, but the generic name is confusable with Beacon Software and others, and no source credits the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Beacons left YC in 2019 but only launched a private beta in September 2020, raised a $6M a16z-led seed in May 2021 and, per aggregators, a $23M Series A in November 2023. It is a crowded link-in-bio market led by Linktree, yet it grew from a free tool into a broader creator business platform with about 25 staff. Funding outcomes are partly unverified and no exit has occurred.
notes: Series A of $23M in November 2023 appears in Clay and CB Insights (both aggregators) but not in a company or press source; recorded as a round per two outlets, flagged as aggregator-based. CB Insights also says $52.35M across 7 rounds, so other rounds likely exist and are not found. Competition as_of set to the private beta launch (2020-09) because the product launched a year after the batch; the TechCrunch competitor list is from February 2021, five months later. Beacons.ai website returned 403. Greg Luppescu comes from a search summary of the seed announcement, not opened directly. Beacon Software (Toronto roll-up, 2026 Series C) is a different company.
